from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            "Think of a drone's flight path.",

        ])

        # Animation elements
        dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
        arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2 + UP*1, color="#FFFF00")

        self.place_at_grid(dot, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, 'C3')

        tip_highlight.next_to(arrow.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'B3')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), Create(dot))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#8888FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"), Create(arrow))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FF88FF"), Create(tip_highlight))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF8800"), Write(label))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Coordinate Representation & Components", 
                          ["We use grids to map space.", "Vectors break into horizontal components.", "They also have vertical components."])
        
        # Setup Grid

        # Components

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Connect the head to the tail.", "This adds two vectors together.", "The result is a new vector."]
        self.setup_layout("Vector Addition: The Head-to-Tail Rule", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define vectors
        origin = np.array([0,0,0])
        u_end = np.array([1.5, 1, 0])
        v_end = np.array([1, 1.5, 0])
        
        u = Arrow(origin, u_end, color=BLUE)
        u_label = MathTex("\\vec{u}", color=BLUE).next_to(u.get_center(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        v = Arrow(origin, v_end, color=YELLOW)
        v_label = MathTex("\\vec{v}", color=YELLOW).next_to(v.get_center(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(u, 'C3')
        self.play(Create(u), Write(u_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        v.shift(u.get_end())
        v_label.next_to(v.get_center(), RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(v), Write(v_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        resultant = Arrow(origin + np.array([1.5, 1, 0]) - np.array([1.5, 1, 0]), u_end + v_end, color=RED)
        resultant.shift(self.grid['C3'] - u.get_start())
        res_label = MathTex("\\vec{u} + \\vec{v}", color=RED).next_to(resultant.get_center(), DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(resultant), Write(res_label))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Scalars stretch or shrink vectors.", "Direction stays same if positive.", "Negative scalars reverse the direction."]
        self.setup_layout("Scalar Multiplication & Scaling", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define base vector
        v = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color="#00FFFF")
        v_label = MathTex(r"\vec{v}", color="#00FFFF").next_to(v, UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(v, v_label), "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(v), Write(v_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Scale v by 2
        v2 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*4, color="#FFFF00")
        v2_label = MathTex(r"2\vec{v}", color="#FFFF00").next_to(v2, UP)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(v2, v2_label), "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(v, v2), ReplacementTransform(v_label, v2_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        # Scale v by -1
        v3 = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=LEFT*2, color="#FF00FF")
        v3_label = MathTex(r"-1\vec{v}", color="#FF00FF").next_to(v3, UP)
        self.place_at_grid(VGroup(v3, v3_label), "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(v2, v3), ReplacementTransform(v2_label, v3_label))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Real-World Application", [
            "Vectors power modern data science.", 
            "Physics engines use them too.", 
            "They map our entire world."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a 2D map overlay with displacement vectors
        dot1 = Dot(color=BLUE)
        dot2 = Dot(color=GREEN)
        vec = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*2, color=YELLOW)
        map_group = VGroup(dot1, dot2, vec)
        self.place_in_area(map_group, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE), Create(map_group))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate a particle following the path of combined vectors
        particle = Dot(color=RED)
        path = VMobject(color=WHITE)
        path.set_points_smoothly([self.grid["D2"], self.grid["E4"], self.grid["D6"]])
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN), MoveAlongPath(particle, path))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display text 'Vectors define movement in space'
        final_text = Text("Vectors define movement in space", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, "F3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW), Write(final_text))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Vectors: The Language of Space
outline.target_audience: High school or introductory university students

sections.title: What is a Vector? (The Intuition)
sections.content: Define a vector as an entity possessing both magnitude and direction, contrasting it with a 'scalar' (magnitude only). Visualize vectors as arrows in a 2D plane.
sections.example: A delivery drone: The scalar is its speed (5 m/s), but the vector includes the direction (North-East), representing its precise flight path.

sections.title: Coordinate Representation & Components
sections.content: Introduce the Cartesian grid. Explain how a vector is decomposed into horizontal (x) and vertical (y) components using unit vectors i and j.
sections.example: Visualizing a character moving on a game map: To reach a treasure at (3, 4), the character moves 3 units along the x-axis and 4 units along the y-axis.

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Head-to-Tail Rule
sections.content: Explain adding vectors geometrically. The head of the first vector connects to the tail of the second, creating a resultant vector.
sections.example: A cat chasing a laser pointer: If the cat moves 2 meters forward and then 3 meters to the right, the resultant vector shows the straight-line displacement from the start.

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication & Scaling
sections.content: Explain how multiplying a vector by a scalar changes its magnitude without changing its direction (or reversing it if negative).
sections.example: A video game character doubling their jump height: The 'jump' vector is multiplied by 2, keeping the same upward direction but stretching the arrow's length.

sections.title: Conclusion and Real-World Application
sections.content: Summarize how these building blocks are the foundation for computer graphics, physics engines, and machine learning, where data points are treated as vectors in high-dimensional space.
sections.example: How search engines use vectors: By representing a search query as a vector, they can find 'nearby' vectors (related topics) in a massive data space.
